result.topic_en: Latin notes on the convergence of the imaginary part of a trigonometric/logarithmic series at rational multiples of 2π (x/2π = m/n), giving finite closed-form values according to whether n is odd or even, followed by a related integral formula with log tan terms.
result.transcription:
Pars imaginaria, cujus seriei convergit, quicunque est valor ipsius $x$, pars realis{+*+}, designantibus $m$, $n$ numeris integris inter se primis, et posito $\frac{x}{2\pi} = \frac{m}{n}$ {+hoc modo+} ita exhiberi potest;
1° si $n$ est [-par-] {+impar+}, aequalis fit,
$\frac{\pi^2}{n^2}\sum_{1,n-1}^{s}(-1)^s \frac{\cos\frac{\pi s}{n}}{\sin\frac{\pi s}{n}^2}\log 4\cos\frac{s m\pi}{n}^2 - \frac{\pi^2}{6^2 n^2}\log 4$
2° si $n$ est par, designante $p$ numerum [-...-] imparem
$= \frac{\pi^2}{n^2}\sum_{\frac{n}{2}-1}^{s} \frac{2(-1)^s\log 4\cos\frac{s m\pi}{n}^2}{\sin\pi\frac{s}{n}^2} + \frac{\pi^2}{3n^2}\log 4 + \frac{2\pi^2}{n^2}(-1)^{\frac{n}{2}}\left(\log\frac{q_0-q}{q_0+q} + \log n + \frac{8}{\pi^2}\sum\frac{\log p}{p^2}\right)$
quae formula [-manifesto-] {+manifesto docet, ita ut intelligatur+} [-convergere-] functionem propositam
[-functionem propositam-]
[-$\frac{2\pi^2}{n^2}$-] subtracta functione $\frac{2\pi^2}{n^2}(-1)^{\frac{n}{2}}\log\frac{q_0-q}{q_0+q}$, si $q$ {+quovis modo stabilito+} convergat versus limitem $q_0$, convergere versus limitem finitum ejus-
que valorem assignat.

Perinde obtinetur
$63)\ \int_0^{e^{xi}} -\log k\,\frac{dq}{q} = -2\log\mathrm{tg}\frac{x}{2}^2 - \frac{2}{9}\log\mathrm{tg}\frac{3x}{2}^2 - \frac{2}{25}\log\mathrm{tg}\frac{5x}{2}^2$


*) si $x$ est {+(quantitas)+} [-numerus-] surdus, non convergit, sin minus, denotan-
do [-literis-] {+literis+} [?] $m$, $n$ numeros integros inter se primos, et ponendo
$\frac{x}{2\pi} = \frac{m}{n}$ ita exhiberi potest

methods.what: Closed-form value of the real part of the series at rational x/2π=m/n with n odd
Value for n even, including a logarithmically divergent term as q→q_0 and a sum over odd p of log p / p^2
Integral of -log k dq/q along to e^{xi} expressed through log tan of odd multiples of x/2

items.quote: Pars imaginaria, cujus seriei convergit, quicunque est valor ipsius $x$
items.english: The imaginary part of this series converges, whatever the value of x.
If x is an irrational (surd) quantity, [the real part] does not converge.

items.quote: quae formula {+manifesto docet, ita ut intelligatur+} [-convergere-] functionem propositam subtracta functione $\frac{2\pi^2}{n^2}(-1)^{\frac{n}{2}}\log\frac{q_0-q}{q_0+q}$, si $q$ {+quovis modo stabilito+} convergat versus limitem $q_0$, convergere versus limitem finitum ejusque valorem assignat.
items.english: This formula clearly shows that the proposed function, after subtracting the function (2π²/n²)(-1)^{n/2} log((q_0-q)/(q_0+q)), converges to a finite limit when q tends in any fixed manner to the limit q_0, and assigns its value.
